feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less duplication across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines communications leadership with Drupal, analytics, workflow design, and multimedia production.  
- Generally clean, professional writing with concrete scale indicators like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: include results such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, campaign impact, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidating would tighten structure and improve scannability.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “cross-channel” and “organization-wide” are consistent, but bullet punctuation and list formatting should be standardized. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with more specific positioning, a cleaner opening, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more modern phrasing.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and sector fit: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Trim channel list detail; those specifics already appear in work experience and skills sections.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The long channel list may feel repetitive given the detailed experience bullets below.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with stronger, CV-aligned phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Prioritize strategic and senior-level capabilities over task-level items; e.g., use “Digital platform modernization” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Consolidate overlapping workflow items into one sharper competency, such as “Editorial systems, governance & workflow design.”
- Suggested version: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Cross-channel communications leadership • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Web platforms & CMS management • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Data analytics & reporting” and “Web & CMS administration” overlap with Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact recent position. Tighten it around scope, ownership, and outcomes, and avoid repeating project detail already covered in Recent Projects.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Serve as strategic communications and digital platforms consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Combine overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance: “Built cross-functional digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing resource hubs.”
- Add measurable scope wherever possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, campaign launches, performance gains, reduced turnaround time, search/discovery improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- The microsite, anniversary campaign, advocacy video, and AI search details already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on role-level leadership and operational impact.
- “Governance/usability/best practices” overlaps with prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new or more senior here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more specific or measurable: add email/social growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign impact; otherwise trim this bullet.
- Tighten operations language: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to strengthen decision-making and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building enterprise capacity/infrastructure.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging during a period of organizational growth.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add views, cadence, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems statement: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” repeats the Director role; use “day-to-day operations” and “editorial coordination” to differentiate.
- “weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic digital/comms phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider changing “Multi-channel” to “Cross-channel” for a more senior, strategic tone.
- Swap “Audience-focused content planning” for “Audience strategy and content planning” to sound more leadership-level.
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “for high-volume public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and implementation strengths rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters tied to recent work: “Drupal platform delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older items unless job-relevant: remove jQuery first; keep SharePoint/Power Pages only if the target role explicitly asks for Microsoft ecosystem experience.
- Put the strongest, most current differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Drupal platform delivery for large public-facing sites” or “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector websites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and dashboarding (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity)”
- Put business-facing skills first: “KPI design,” “executive/leadership reporting,” and “performance analysis” signal seniority better than leading with platforms.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for clearer, more standard phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work elsewhere, such as “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; consider making Topline Skills more strategic and leaving tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and tied to delivery environments rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Live Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and in-house studio systems
- Virtual event technical direction and show operations
- If accurate, strengthen with scale/scope language: “broadcast-quality,” “in-house studio,” “recurring advocacy programming,” or “large-format conference/event production.”
- Keep tools out unless they add differentiation; this section should signal capability, not repeat software lists from Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is partly duplicated by “Premiere Pro” and “Podcast production” in Technical + IT.
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies; use broader phrasing here to avoid repetition.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, which is central to recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add level/context if format allows: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If you want stronger impact, replace weaker/older tools with evidence-based phrasing: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views) • WordPress • SharePoint**
- Keep it concise; avoid listing platforms with little demonstrated use unless they support target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is largely duplicated by **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider merging or making one broader and one more outcome-focused.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise platforms unless it supports a specific project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and aligned to the recent Drupal/AI/search/automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten phrasing and modernize terms: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, REST/API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add context-setting qualifiers instead of just tools: Front-end development, API integrations, tag management, edge/serverless scripting, CI/CD workflows
- Consider a stronger final version: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (CI/CD)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one version broader and this one more tool-specific.
- If Cloudflare Workers/GitHub Actions are not used in recent roles, consider removing to avoid over-weighting older or lighter-use tools.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads like a generic software list. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere, so it should emphasize systems most relevant to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and tighten to higher-signal tools: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project operations: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Remove lower-priority or older tools unless they were central recently; Basecamp and Trello look less relevant than current enterprise-stack tools.
- If accurate, add scope in a parenthetical to show applied use, e.g., “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automations).”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” to better match the actual content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same positioning verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are generic collaboration tools; keep only if space allows or if they were operationally important.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership implied in recent roles. It should signal enterprise email operations rather than just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Enterprise newsletter and audience engagement platforms**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Used to support high-volume member communications, newsletter operations and campaign engagement**
- Keep platform names only if these are systems you directly administered or used strategically; otherwise remove weaker/older tools

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands”; avoid repeating audience scale here unless you add a distinct angle such as platform administration, segmentation, automation, or campaign workflows.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate core competencies; make the label more platform-specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and the website refresh.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence around 2–3 core contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day digital workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “helped oversee daily work of a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early producing rather than expanding.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple roles; specify what changed or omit.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later digital/media roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since those better demonstrate senior digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media entries; keep this focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here, since that becomes stronger and more relevant in 2015–2024 roles.
